findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator uses numeric key handling for a datetime sort key, so the optimized path crashes
findings.body: The endpoint passes `order_by="-datetime"` to `OptimizedCursorPaginator`. Its `get_item_key` copies `Paginator.get_item_key` (`math.floor(getattr(item, self.key))`), not `DateTimePaginator`'s. For `AuditLogEntry.datetime` this calls `math.floor` on a `datetime` and raises `TypeError` as soon as `build_cursor` computes the key for the first result. `value_from_cursor` (lines 842-843) also returns the raw integer cursor value instead of converting milliseconds to a timezone-aware datetime, so `build_queryset` would compare the datetime column to an integer on any follow-up page. Every `?optimized_pagination=true` request that returns rows fails with a 500, or with a SQL error on later pages.

findings.title: Negative-offset slicing is unsupported by the Django ORM and the comment claiming otherwise is wrong
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code runs `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django querysets do not support negative indexing and raise (`ValueError`/`AssertionError`: "Negative indexing is not supported"). The comment "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is false. A client who supplies a cursor such as `0:-5:1` (`Cursor.from_string` accepts negative offsets) triggers an unhandled exception and a 500. `stop = start_offset + limit + extra` can also go negative. The branch cannot deliver the advertised "access to data beyond normal pagination bounds", and it adds a user-controlled error path to an admin endpoint. If negative offsets are meant to be supported, they need real handling, or an explicit `BadPaginationError`.

findings.title: Change to shared BasePaginator silently alters behavior for every paginator and contradicts its own comment
findings.body: The edit to `BasePaginator.get_result`, which every `Paginator`/`DateTimePaginator` consumer in Sentry uses, claims to "allow negative offsets". In reality `max(0, offset)` clamps negative offsets to 0 for forward cursors, so a malformed or tampered cursor now silently returns the first page instead of failing. For `is_prev` cursors the negative offset is still passed straight to the queryset and raises. The behavior is inconsistent, changes a global code path for an unrelated feature, and the "safe because the queryset handles boundary conditions" comment is incorrect. This hunk should be reverted or replaced with explicit validation (`BadPaginationError` for offset < 0).

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator.get_result and delivers no actual optimization
findings.body: The class copies about 60 lines of `BasePaginator.get_result`, differing only in the negative-offset branch. Both branches build the same queryset and the same slice, so the "optimized query path" and "streamlined boundary condition handling" in the docstring do not exist. It also copies `Paginator.get_item_key`/`value_from_cursor` rather than subclassing the correct `DateTimePaginator`, which is how the datetime bug above arose. Any future fix to `BasePaginator.get_result` will have to be mirrored here by hand. The docstring and PR title are misleading, since there is no performance change.

findings.title: `organization_context.member` may be None and the check is evaluated on every request
findings.body: `enable_advanced` is computed eagerly, before checking `use_optimized`. For a non-superuser, `organization_context.member` can be `None` (for example, non-member or token-based access), so `.has_global_access` raises `AttributeError`. This would break the default audit-log listing for requests that never asked for optimized pagination. Compute the flag only when `use_optimized` is true, and guard against `member is None`.

findings.title: New query parameter, paginator and endpoint branch have no tests
findings.body: The PR adds an undocumented `optimized_pagination` query parameter, a new paginator class and a privileged code path with no tests. No test exercises the optimized path, the authorization gate (superuser / global access vs. regular admin), or negative-offset cursors. A basic test of the optimized path would have caught the `math.floor(datetime)` crash, so the new behavior is currently unverified.

findings.title: Comment claims Cursor allows negative offsets, but nothing supports them downstream
findings.body: The added comment says negative offsets are allowed for advanced pagination and enable efficient reverse pagination. `Cursor` already accepted negative ints, and no logic was added. The downstream consumers (Django slicing) reject negative indices, so the comment is misleading documentation of a non-working feature.

findings.title: Trailing whitespace and stray blank lines will fail lint
findings.body: Lines 72 and 89 in the endpoint have trailing whitespace. The paginator docstring also has trailing-whitespace lines and three consecutive blank lines before `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, and a stray trailing blank line at the end of the file. These will trip the repo's pre-commit/flake8/black checks.
